verdict.rationale: WooCommerce's extensibility is built on WordPress's native PHP hook system (add_action/add_filter), documented in the Storefront guide, and reinforced by a marketplace of extensions and REST/webhook APIs for custom integrations — this hook architecture is the mechanism developers use to inject custom discount, shipping, and validation logic that runs inside the platform. However, the evidence pack only shows hooks in the context of theme template rendering (docs-9/45), not explicit documentation of hooking into checkout/shipping/discount calculation pipelines, and there is no serverless-function execution model (WooCommerce runs as a monolithic PHP plugin, not serverless). Missing for 10: explicit documentation of core WooCommerce action/filter hooks for cart/discount/shipping/validation logic (e.g. woocommerce_cart_calculate_fees, custom shipping method classes), and any serverless/function-as-a-service execution model.
